prompt: One hundred jobs are independently assigned to one hundred uniformly selected servers. Why can many servers remain idle despite the average being one job per server?

options.text: Random assignment allows repeated choices and uneven occupancy.
options.explanation: Several jobs can choose one server while another is never chosen.

options.text: An average of one guarantees one at every server.
options.explanation: The mean across servers does not specify each individual occupancy.

options.text: Each job is required to choose an unused server.
options.explanation: That would be sampling without replacement, a different model.

options.text: Idle servers imply the total job count changed.
options.explanation: The same total work can be distributed unevenly.

workedExample: Track one server: it is idle if every job misses it. Independent choices give that a positive probability. Summing idle-server indicators counts the expected empty servers without contradicting the fixed average occupancy.

link.title: Introduction to Probability — Grinstead and Snell

prompt: Under independent uniform hashing, which approaches correctly analyse the indicated quantity? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use one indicator per bucket to count empty buckets.
options.explanation: Each indicator asks whether all keys miss that bucket.

options.text: Use one indicator per unordered key pair to count colliding pairs.
options.explanation: Each indicator asks whether that pair shares a bucket.

options.text: Use the mean occupancy of one bucket as the maximum occupancy.
options.explanation: A maximum is a different quantity and is not given by that mean.

options.text: Use one indicator per key to count occupancy of a specified bucket.
options.explanation: Each indicator asks whether that key lands in the selected bucket.

workedExample: Choose the units you are counting before writing indicators: keys, empty buckets or pairs. Linearity applies to their sums even when bucket events are dependent. It does not turn a mean into a maximum.
